definition: An attack that attempts to determine whether a specific data point was part of a model's training dataset.
details: Membership inference attacks are a privacy concern for models trained on sensitive data, and defenses like differential privacy are designed in part to mitigate this risk.

explainer.lead: An attack that tries to determine whether a specific data point was part of a model's training dataset. It is a privacy concern for models trained on sensitive data, and defenses like differential privacy are designed in part to mitigate it.

tiers.eli5: Someone tries to work out whether your name was in the pile of papers the model studied, by probing how it answers about you.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers assess membership inference risk when models are trained on sensitive data and use differential privacy among the defenses aimed at reducing it.
tiers.paperLevel: An attack that attempts to determine whether a specific data point was part of a model's training dataset; defenses such as differential privacy are designed in part to mitigate this risk.

explainer.example: An attacker queries a model about a particular record and uses the response to judge whether that record was in its training set.
